method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021' (published 21 April 2022), 23 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC9325452). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (Haematology Reference Committee) 'eviQ cutaneous T-cell lymphoma protocols (not guidelines): 4556 mogamulizumab (v.1, first approved 22 October 2025), 1391 vorinostat (v.3, last reviewed 11 November 2022) and 1665 brentuximab vedotin (v.6, last reviewed 28 April 2023)' (retrieved 24 September 2026 (review due: 4556 and 1391 31 December 2026; 1665 30 June 2027)), 7 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0. eviQ also states that "eviQ content should not be hosted on external sites", and that commercial entities must contact eviQ to seek permission (read at https://www.eviq.org.au/copyright (Disclaimer and copyright page)). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. The stage-by-stage treatment tables (Tables 7 and 8) and diagnostic/staging tables were stripped; claims rest on the narrative text. Edition 2.0 keeps every S2k 2021 claim (S1) unchanged and adds S2, three Australian eviQ protocols (CC BY-NC 4.0, paraphrased), for mogamulizumab, vorinostat and brentuximab vedotin doses, PBS status and safety monitoring. The S2 source file concatenates the protocol pages (https://www.eviq.org.au/p/4556, /p/1391 and /p/1665), each under a header line naming its URL; only protocol text from the ID line to the literature-search section was kept. eviQ asks that adaptations cite the eviQ ID, version and URL, as given in the S2 title and those URLs. Table rows appended with pmc_text.py --append-tables (2026-09-24); claims from S1 Table 3 (imaging for first staging), the boxed diagnostic recommendation labelled Table 4 by position, and Table 8 (Sézary syndrome treatment). S1 Tables 2, 4–7, 9, 10a–b and 11a–d could not be extracted (ragged rows or merged cells), so the MF stage-by-stage table is still missing.

claims.claim: **Cutaneous lymphomas arise in the skin with no other organ involved at staging**; about 73% are T-cell types. They must be told apart from skin spread of nodal lymphoma or leukaemia, which is managed very differently.
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Manage jointly between a specialist centre and the primary doctor.**
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Clinical findings often suggest the diagnosis, but confirm it with histology, immunohistology and molecular tests**; examine the whole skin and every lymph node region.
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stage MF and SS with the revised TNMB system.** Early MF (IA-IIA) usually carries a very good outlook, with mean survival of about 10 to 20 years.
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Work-up at first staging (S1 Table 3):** for MF and its variants, a chest X-ray with abdominal and lymph node ultrasound; from stage IIB onwards, and in Sézary syndrome, a contrast CT of neck, chest, abdomen and pelvis with lymph node ultrasound, adding PET-CT where indicated. Use flow cytometry if blood involvement is suspected, and include clonality testing in the diagnosis. Re-staging after treatment, at progression and in aggressive types is tailored to the patient.
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat by entity and stage, and keep treatment restrained** for the common CTCL types.
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In early stages, prefer skin-directed options:** topical steroids, phototherapy, topical chlormethine (or carmustine), bexarotene gel or imiquimod.
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Phototherapy for stages IA-IIA:** narrow-band UVB (311 nm) or PUVA. Reserve PUVA mainly for thick plaques or folliculotropic MF; either suits erythrodermic MF.
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Radiotherapy:** for localised CTCL, at least 30 Gy in 2 Gy fractions controls 90-100% of lesions long term. Low-dose palliative radiotherapy (8 Gy, given as one or two fractions) gave complete remission in at least 92%.
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Total skin electron beam:** conventional doses (30-36 Gy) work but are harsher on the skin; low-dose 10-12 Gy over 2-3 weeks is a safer short-term option, followed by maintenance treatment.
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Advanced stages call for systemic treatment**, typically PUVA combined with a retinoid or interferon-alpha; bexarotene is also recommended.
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Conventional interferon-alpha (Roferon) is no longer available;** pegylated interferon is used off-label; in a small series peginterferon alfa-2a at 180 μg weekly worked as well as higher doses. Start at a moderate dose and watch for liver and marrow toxicity.
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Brentuximab vedotin is an option for advanced CD30-positive MF** (tumour stage).
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mogamulizumab (anti-CCR4, approved 2019) is a second-line systemic option** for refractory or advanced MF and for SS after at least one prior systemic therapy; it works especially well on blood involvement.
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **HDAC inhibitors (vorinostat, romidepsin) and pralatrexate are alternatives** approved in the USA rather than Europe.
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: 🇦🇺 **Mogamulizumab (eviQ ID 4556), for relapsed or refractory MF or SS after at least one systemic therapy:** 1 mg/kg IV on days 1, 8, 15 and 22 of the first 28-day cycle, then on days 1 and 15 of later cycles, until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Give each dose within 2 days of its date; if more than 2 days late, give it as soon as possible and restart the schedule from then. PBS Authority; premedication is required.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (Haematology Reference Committee), 'eviQ cutaneous T-cell lymphoma protocols (not guidelines): 4556 mogamulizumab (v.1, first approved 22 October 2025), 1391 vorinostat (v.3, last reviewed 11 November 2022) and 1665 brentuximab vedotin (v.6, last reviewed 28 April 2023)', retrieved 24 September 2026 (review due: 4556 and 1391 31 December 2026; 1665 30 June 2027), https://www.eviq.org.au/haematology/lymphoma/nk-cell-and-t-cell-lymphoma, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Mogamulizumab rash can mimic progression:** it takes many forms (papular, lichenoid, granulomatous, psoriasiform and others), so consider a skin biopsy to tell drug eruption from disease; SJS and TEN, some fatal, have occurred. Watch for immune-mediated harm (myositis, myocarditis, hepatitis, pneumonitis, Guillain-Barré, hypothyroidism; consider thyroid tests) and high blood sugar.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (Haematology Reference Committee), 'eviQ cutaneous T-cell lymphoma protocols (not guidelines): 4556 mogamulizumab (v.1, first approved 22 October 2025), 1391 vorinostat (v.3, last reviewed 11 November 2022) and 1665 brentuximab vedotin (v.6, last reviewed 28 April 2023)', retrieved 24 September 2026 (review due: 4556 and 1391 31 December 2026; 1665 30 June 2027), https://www.eviq.org.au/haematology/lymphoma/nk-cell-and-t-cell-lymphoma, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Mogamulizumab before an allogeneic transplant raises the risk of severe and steroid-refractory GVHD and transplant death,** more so when given within about 50 days of the transplant; watch closely for early GVHD.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (Haematology Reference Committee), 'eviQ cutaneous T-cell lymphoma protocols (not guidelines): 4556 mogamulizumab (v.1, first approved 22 October 2025), 1391 vorinostat (v.3, last reviewed 11 November 2022) and 1665 brentuximab vedotin (v.6, last reviewed 28 April 2023)', retrieved 24 September 2026 (review due: 4556 and 1391 31 December 2026; 1665 30 June 2027), https://www.eviq.org.au/haematology/lymphoma/nk-cell-and-t-cell-lymphoma, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: 🇦🇺 **Vorinostat (eviQ ID 1391), for relapsed or chemotherapy-refractory CTCL:** 400 mg by mouth once a day until progression or unacceptable toxicity (100 mg capsules; PBS Authority). If it is not tolerated, drop to 300 mg once a day with or just after food, then if needed to 300 mg on 5 consecutive days each week.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (Haematology Reference Committee), 'eviQ cutaneous T-cell lymphoma protocols (not guidelines): 4556 mogamulizumab (v.1, first approved 22 October 2025), 1391 vorinostat (v.3, last reviewed 11 November 2022) and 1665 brentuximab vedotin (v.6, last reviewed 28 April 2023)', retrieved 24 September 2026 (review due: 4556 and 1391 31 December 2026; 1665 30 June 2027), https://www.eviq.org.au/haematology/lymphoma/nk-cell-and-t-cell-lymphoma, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Vorinostat safety (eviQ):** it can prolong the QT interval (correct electrolytes, avoid other QT drugs, consider ECG and electrolyte checks), causes venous thromboembolism, and can dehydrate through diarrhoea and vomiting; patients should drink at least 2 L a day. Check blood count, kidney and liver tests, calcium, magnesium, phosphate and glucose at baseline, fortnightly over the first 2 months, and 4-weekly after that.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (Haematology Reference Committee), 'eviQ cutaneous T-cell lymphoma protocols (not guidelines): 4556 mogamulizumab (v.1, first approved 22 October 2025), 1391 vorinostat (v.3, last reviewed 11 November 2022) and 1665 brentuximab vedotin (v.6, last reviewed 28 April 2023)', retrieved 24 September 2026 (review due: 4556 and 1391 31 December 2026; 1665 30 June 2027), https://www.eviq.org.au/haematology/lymphoma/nk-cell-and-t-cell-lymphoma, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: 🇦🇺 **Brentuximab vedotin (eviQ ID 1665) for relapsed or refractory CD30-positive CTCL** (MF, SS or primary cutaneous ALCL): 1.8 mg/kg IV (capped at 180 mg) every 21 days for up to 16 cycles; PBS Authority. Assess neuropathy before every dose (grade 2 or worse may need a lower dose, delay or omission) and watch for PML, pancreatitis and severe skin reactions.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (Haematology Reference Committee), 'eviQ cutaneous T-cell lymphoma protocols (not guidelines): 4556 mogamulizumab (v.1, first approved 22 October 2025), 1391 vorinostat (v.3, last reviewed 11 November 2022) and 1665 brentuximab vedotin (v.6, last reviewed 28 April 2023)', retrieved 24 September 2026 (review due: 4556 and 1391 31 December 2026; 1665 30 June 2027), https://www.eviq.org.au/haematology/lymphoma/nk-cell-and-t-cell-lymphoma, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Before any of these protocols (eviQ):** screen for hepatitis B (HBsAg, anti-HBc and anti-HBs), and avoid live vaccines in moderately or severely immunocompromised patients.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW (Haematology Reference Committee), 'eviQ cutaneous T-cell lymphoma protocols (not guidelines): 4556 mogamulizumab (v.1, first approved 22 October 2025), 1391 vorinostat (v.3, last reviewed 11 November 2022) and 1665 brentuximab vedotin (v.6, last reviewed 28 April 2023)', retrieved 24 September 2026 (review due: 4556 and 1391 31 December 2026; 1665 30 June 2027), https://www.eviq.org.au/haematology/lymphoma/nk-cell-and-t-cell-lymphoma, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Prefer single-agent chemotherapy** (for example low-dose gemcitabine or doxorubicin) to combination regimens, which cause heavy immunosuppression without improving survival.
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Extracorporeal photopheresis works in SS with few side effects**, alone or with interferon-alpha, PUVA, topical steroids or bexarotene.
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Second-choice options in SS:** bexarotene or low-dose methotrexate (ideally with PUVA and photopheresis), or total skin electron beam. Doxorubicin or gemcitabine can debulk advanced SS; use alemtuzumab at low doses to limit infection.
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **S1's Sézary syndrome table (order within each column is not a ranking):** first choice is extracorporeal photopheresis, combined as needed with PUVA, interferon-alpha and/or bexarotene, or else PUVA with interferon-alpha and/or bexarotene. Second choice: mogamulizumab; chlorambucil with a steroid (the Winkelmann regimen); low-dose methotrexate; bexarotene; total skin electron beam; alemtuzumab (IV, or low-dose subcutaneous); doxorubicin, fludarabine, cladribine or gemcitabine; allogeneic stem cell transplant for selected patients; or brentuximab vedotin (off-label).
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Allogeneic stem cell transplant may suit selected patients.** Palliative chemotherapy in late stages has no proven survival benefit and adds infection risk.
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After remission or down-staging of advanced disease, maintain with the guideline's non-cytotoxic treatments.**
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For itch (off-label):** in CTCL, gabapentin 300 to 2400 mg/day, or mirtazapine 7.5-30 mg taken at bedtime; in SS, aprepitant 80 mg/day.
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Follow-up aims to catch relapse, second lymphomas and treatment harms** (such as PUVA-related skin cancers). Teach every patient to check their own skin and feel their lymph nodes regularly.
claims.locator: German Dermatological Society / German Cancer Society guideline group (Dippel E, Assaf C, Becker JC, et al.), Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft, 'S2k-Guidelines – Cutaneous lymphomas (ICD10 C82 - C86): Update 2021', published 21 April 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9325452/, retrieved 2026-09-23
